articles.title: Philip Rivers Hires Former NFL Assistant Coach as NC State Offensive Coordinator
articles.summary: NC State has hired Jason Michael as the team's offensive coordinator under new head coach Philip Rivers, the school announced Wednesday.
articles.body:
NC State has hired Jason Michael as the team's offensive coordinator under new head coach Philip Rivers, the school announced Wednesday.

Rivers, who played for the Wolfpack in college before earning eight Pro Bowl nods across his NFL career with the Los Angeles Chargers and Indianapolis Colts, was officially hired as the head coach of his alma mater on Nov. 11.

"I'm really excited to add coach Michael to our staff," Rivers said, per the school's official website . "I have history with him from my time with the Chargers and with the Colts and we are aligned in our vision for building this program. His expertise and experience in the offensive system that we are going to implement here at NC State is second to none, and I can't wait for him to get started."

Michael has coached at the NFL level since 2009, recently operating as the Philadelphia Eagles' tight ends coach from 2021-25.

He has familiarity with Rivers, serving as the Chargers' tight ends coach alongside the star quarterback from 2011-13. Michael was also a member of the Colts' coaching staff in 2020 while Rivers was with the team.

Michael has two years of experience as an offensive coordinator, filling the role for the Tennessee Titans from 2014-15.

The Titans struggled during his tenure, ranking No. 30 among all NFL teams in scoring offense during the 2014 season before ranking No. 28 in 2015.

NC State is looking to establish itself as a threat in the ACC under Rivers after compiling a mere 18-18 record since the start of the 2024 season. That includes a 4-6 mark this year.

articles.title: Juliano Belletti hits back at claims Jesse Bisiwu is struggling to adapt at Barcelona
articles.summary: The coach has backed the summer signing.
articles.body:
Bisiwu impressed in pre-season and had been expected to share game time with Belletti's men and Hansi Flick's first team this season.

An early injury disrupted his progress and there has been talk he's struggling to settle. Belletti's been asked about such talk and insisted the youngster is doing fine.

"Who said that? From day one he has been adapted, very happy and very happy to be with us. In every training session he listens, asks questions, tries to adapt to the way of playing, especially since we have wingers in width, which comes a bit inside," he told Sport.

"He is searching, asking, and I always see very good intentions on his part as well, especially in defensive transitions.

"He is adapting to our way of playing and evolving a lot, especially as a footballer, in the discipline of playing without the ball. Not integrated? On the contrary, here in our daily lives, Bisiwu is adapted and very happy."

articles.title: Fred Warner's heritage makes 49ers' upcoming game in Mexico City special
articles.summary: (AP) — San Francisco has a history with Mexico, having played there in 2022, while 49ers linebacker Fred Warner has roots in the country.Warner’s maternal gr...
articles.body:
AIR FORCE ACADEMY, Colo. (AP) — San Francisco has a history with Mexico, having played there in 2022, while 49ers linebacker Fred Warner has roots in the country.

Warner's maternal grandfather was born in Mexico but died when Warner's mother, Laura, was young. Although he never met his grandfather, Warner has spoken in the past about his connection to Mexican culture, including speaking Spanish in his childhood home.

San Francisco plays the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday night, and Warner is excited to return.

"Super special," he said after practice on Wednesday. "I remember that first time around, didn't know what exactly what to expect, but I think that was my first time being out of the country and playing in a game of that magnitude."

Warner attended a World Cup game at Estadio Azteca last summer and found the atmosphere electric.

"That was elite," said Warner, who leads the team in tackles with 88. "Soccer, or football as they call it, the World Cup, representing your home country, that is a whole different animal. The NFL obviously is elite as well, but that was that was a once-in-a-lifetime experience."

San Francisco beat Arizona 38-10 in Mexico City on Nov. 21, 2022, and the team is following the same blueprint to prepare for Sunday night's game. After beating Dallas last Sunday, the 49ers flew to Colorado so they could practice at the Air Force Academy, where the 7,258-foot elevation is nearly equal to Mexico City, hoping to gain an advantage for the NFL's final international game of 2026.

They hope some things are different from four years ago.

"Usually our last bus of players gets three hours before the game, and they got lost somehow on the way to the stadium," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "They didn't get there until an hour and 15 minutes before the game, and had like 12 starters on it. So that was somewhat stressful, but it didn't affect us.

"After the game it took us about 10 hours to get out of there, just because we had to wait through customs for the Cardinals to go first, so we got back the next Tuesday morning at like 9 a.m. because we played on a Monday night. The stadium was awesome. The atmosphere is great. It was a really cool place to play football."

Evans could return to practice soon and other injury news

Wide receiver Mike Evans did not practice Wednesday but has not been ruled out for Sunday night, Shanahan said. Evans, who has missed the last three games with Achilles tendinitis, is third on the team in catches (39) and receiving yards (420) despite playing in just six of nine games.

"Hopefully he'll be able to go (Thursday)," Shanahan said. "I'm not sure yet, but taking it day by day right now."

Evans did some work with two coaches in pre-practice warmups, lightly jogging while catching passes near the sideline on a windy afternoon.

Evans, in his first season with San Francisco, has made an impact when available, most notably his seven catches for 113 yards and a score in a Week 5 win at Seattle despite playing with a rib injury.

Shanahan was asked if Evans' presence in Colorado means there's hope he can play Sunday night.

"Haven't thought about that," he said. "Maybe, but he does have a chance. But, if he didn't, probably still would've brought him."

Linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) also did not practice but Shanahan said he is likely to practice Thursday. Cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Upton Stout (shoulder), safeties Ji'Ayir Brown (ankle) and Siran Neal (foot) and defensive end Khalid Kareem (ankle) were limited.

articles.title: Miami Hurricanes Must Win To Secure Playoff Spot
articles.summary: Miami sits at No. 7 but needs the ACC title for a playoff bid. Can the Canes handle Virginia Tech and Boston College to keep their dream alive?
articles.body:
Following Saturday's 36-25 victory against Duke, the Miami Hurricanes remain fixed at No. 7 in the newest College Football Playoff rankings. The Selection Committee revealed these numbers on Tuesday, and the Canes did not move up. Notre Dame and Texas swapped spots, but Miami stayed put. The team lost to Notre Dame 31-24 earlier in the season, and that loss to the only ranked opponent on their schedule hurts their case. They need a clear path forward to make the playoff.

Winning the Atlantic Coast Conference title is the only sure way to get an automatic bid. Under the 12 team format the four highest ranked conference champions earn a first-round bye, which Miami in that position if it wins the league. The path is narrow. Wake Forest sits at No. 11 after a huge 49-7 win over SMU. Were the playoffs to begin now, the Demon Deacons would secure the final spot via an at-large bid. Miami has to beat teams in front of them to climb higher.

Maintaining an undefeated conference record, Miami retains the opportunity to reach the playoff for a second consecutive year. They face Virginia Tech on Nov. 21 and Boston College on Nov. 28. Both games are at Hard Rock Stadium. According to reports, the Canes hold better than a 95% probability of winning both upcoming games. That is a good sign, but the stats do not guarantee a win on the field.

Should Miami finish the regular season undefeated yet fall in the conference title game, their likelihood of securing an at-large bid probably vanishes. An ACC champion carrying two non-conference losses will struggle to earn votes from the committee. The team must win the ACC Championship to lock in a spot. They appeared in the title game in 2017 but lost to Clemson 38-3. They have never won that game.

Wide receiver Malachi Toney remains unavailable for the Hurricanes due to ankle surgery. He is a star player, and his health matters for the final stretch. The dream is to have him back for the semifinals or a potential rematch with Notre Dame. The committee chair Hunter Yurachek said, "It's hard for me to sit here with two weeks left in the regular season and of course championship weekend to say what can happen with Miami in the rankings and those above them," according to Sports Illustrated .

Yurachek also noted that losses by teams above Miami would help the Canes as long as they keep winning. He added, "Obviously, if there's some movement or losses in teams above them, that helps them as long as they continue to win. Then of course if they advance to the ACC championship game, if it is indeed Wake Forest, they have an opportunity against a ranked team on championship weekend." The Hurricanes will aim to win the ACC Championship in Charlotte, N.C. on Dec. 5, 2026.

If they win the title game and finish as one of the top-four conference champions, they get a bye in the first round and set their first playoff game for New Year's. That gives the team more rest while other talented players come out of the injury booth. The committee says Miami will likely stay in the six-to-eight range unless something drastic happens.

articles.title: Utah Royals' Jimmy Coenraets wins NWSL coach of the year
articles.summary: WASHINGTON, D.C. — Utah Royals head coach Jimmy Coenraets won the 2026 National Women’s Soccer League Coach of the Year after a remarkable turnaround for a c...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Utah Royals head coach Jimmy Coenraets won the 2026 National Women's Soccer League Coach of the Year after a remarkable turnaround for a club that went from one of the NWSL's worst teams to a playoff team in the space of a season.

The 31-year-old Belgian beat out San Diego Wave head coach Jonas Eidevall and Gotham FC's Juan Carlos Amorós for the honor, announced Wednesday during the league's annual awards ceremony at Lisner Auditorium in Washington, D.C.

The Belgian is hardly a conventional coach.

Coenraets played soccer growing up but could not complete his dreams of becoming a pro because of a heart condition. He then studied marketing and has a master's degree in strategy and international football business. While initially inclined to focus on the business of soccer, his passion for the sport eventually led him to coach for OH Leuven in Belgium.

When the assistant coach offer came from Utah's then-sporting director, Kelly Cousins, he jumped at the opportunity.

Coenraets, one of the youngest head coaches in the league, guided the Royals to their first playoff appearance since the franchise returned to the NWSL in 2024 after finishing 12th in the standings last season. Utah produced one of the biggest upsets of the postseason, eliminating the higher-seeded Wave in the quarterfinals before falling 2-1 to the Washington Spirit in Saturday's semifinal.

But the team's transformation began long before the playoffs.

Coenraets inherited a club struggling to establish itself after its 2023 relocation. The Royals struggled to sign big stars, but rather than relying on established standouts, Coenraets focused on building a collective identity, developing younger players and instilling a competitive mentality that made Utah increasingly difficult to beat.

"If you look at the way we play as a team right now, that's not 100 percent how I'm used to playing," Coenraets told The Athletic earlier this year. "But it does suit what we have, where we are as a franchise, and it suits within the plan of where we want to go."

The Royals emerged as one of the surprises of the regular season, climbing into the upper reaches of the standings and establishing themselves as legitimate postseason contenders. Coenraets was named NWSL Coach of the Month in May, an early indication of the progress his team was making.

articles.title: Prosecutors Drop Some Charges Against NC State's Ex-Head Trainer Accused of Sex Abuse of Athletes
articles.summary: RALEIGH, N.C. (AP) — Prosecutors have dismissed 10 misdemeanor charges against N.C. State's former director of sports medicine, who's accused of sexually abusing former Wolfpack male athletes under the guise of treatment.
articles.body:
RALEIGH, N.C. (AP) — Prosecutors have dismissed 10 misdemeanor charges against N.C. State's former director of sports medicine, who's accused of sexually abusing former Wolfpack male athletes under the guise of treatment.

Robert M. Murphy Jr. was arrested in September in Florida on out-of-state fugitive warrants from North Carolina. That came after a grand jury indicted him on nine felony counts of sexual contact under pretext of medical treatment and 23 misdemeanor counts of sexual battery.

Indictments were tied to allegations ranging from October 2016 to fall 2021. But Murphy's attorneys had sought to dismiss some charges as outside a two-year statute of limitations while also arguing that a 2019 revision to state law extending that clock applies only going forward.

Prosecutors ultimately agreed in dismissing 10 charges, according to court filings from Tuesday. The other charges remain.

The criminal case originated with a federal civil lawsuit from a single athlete filed four years ago . That complaint alleged years of misconduct by Murphy, such as improper touching of the genitals during massages and intrusive observation while collecting urine samples during drug testing.

That grew to more than 30 athletes outlining allegations in years of civil lawsuits . Murphy's attorneys have denied wrongdoing by their client.

articles.title: Premier League champions Leicester City cut ties with sponsor after porn actress appointment sparks fan backlash
articles.summary: Leicester City have parted ways with front-of-shirt sponsor BC Game after the gambling firm's appointment of Russian porn actress Eva Elfie as a brand
articles.body: Leicester City have parted ways with front-of-shirt sponsor BC Game after the gambling firm's appointment of Russian porn actress Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador triggered a backlash from supporters of the former Premier League champions.The League One club announced on Wednesday that the commercial partnership, which began at the start of the 2024-25 season, had been terminated with immediate effect following discussions between the two parties."Leicester City Football Club and BC.GAME have reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect," the club said in a statement. "The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward."BC Game announced Elfie as its brand ambassador earlier this month, posting a promotional video featuring the Russian adult film actor and a delivery driver on social media with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin."The appointment drew criticism from Leicester supporters, with the Foxes Trust Supporters Group questioning the club's association with a gambling company that had now brought pornography into its brand promotions.Fans question Leicester's association with gambling and pornographyThe supporters' group had expressed its opposition to the sponsorship arrangement even before the latest development, arguing that both gambling and pornography could have harmful consequences, particularly for young people."From the moment the club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company, we felt Leicester City were ditching its values," the Foxes Trust said in a statement on November 4. "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City."Is this who we are now?"The club's decision to end the partnership comes after the growing criticism surrounding BC Game's choice of ambassador. Leicester also confirmed an enhanced returns policy for supporters who had purchased shirts carrying the sponsor's branding.Under the arrangement, fans who bought BC Game-branded shirts since October 21 can seek an exchange or refund, even if the shirts have been worn or personalised.The club also thanked BC Game for the "constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement".From Premier League champions to League OneThe sponsorship controversy comes during a difficult period for Leicester, whose remarkable Premier League triumph in the 2015-16 season remains one of English football's most celebrated underdog stories.Having defied the odds to lift the title, the Midlands club have since endured a dramatic decline, suffering back-to-back relegations and dropping into the third tier of English football.The end of the BC Game association marks another significant off-field development for a club seeking to rebuild its fortunes.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pablo Sarabia: "A Mourinho le estaré eternamente agradecido"
articles.standfirst: El ex jugador de Real Madrid, Getafe, Sevilla o PSG, internacional en 27 ocasiones con España y, actualmente, en Al Arabi de la Qatar Stars League, atiende a MARCA para repasar su trayectoria
articles.summary: El ex jugador de Real Madrid, Getafe, Sevilla o PSG, internacional en 27 ocasiones con España y, actualmente, en Al Arabi de la Qatar Stars League, atiende a MARCA para repasar su trayectoria
articles.body: Pablo Sarabia (Madrid, 1992) fue uno de esos 'mirlos' a los que, antes de 'volar' de La Fábrica, Mourinho le dio la oportunidad de debutar en el Santiago Bernabéu... y en un partido de Champions contra el Auxerre en diciembre de 2012. Fuera del Real Madrid hace frío. Pero maduró en el Getafe, explotó en el Sevilla y firmó por un transatlántico como el PSG. También representó a la Selección en 27 ocasiones, incluyendo la Eurocopa 2021 y el Mundial 2022. Ahora, en las filas de Al Arabi de la Qatar Stars League, atiende a MARCA para repasar una carrera que todavía sigue muy vigente. PREGUNTA. Segunda temporada en Qatar. ¿Ya completamente adaptado a la vida en Oriente Medio? RESPUESTA. Sí, totalmente. Ha sido muy fácil la adaptación. La verdad es que la gente es muy hospitalaria e intenta ayudarte en todo. Ha sido muy sencillo a nivel de club y de vida. P. ¿El nivel de la Qatar Stars League superó sus expectativas antes de llegar? Hay jugadores bastante contrastados: Brozovic, Verratti, Firmino, Mahrez… R. Las ha superado. También me he encontrado con una Liga que tiene una cosa muy buena: la competitividad entre todos los equipos es muy alta. Puedes perder contra el colista y ganarle al líder. También hay jugadores muy buenos, obviamente. Pero creo que el mayor acierto es contrastar esos nombres con el nivel competitivo de todos los jugadores. P. Fue campeón de Europa Sub19 y Sub21 con Lopetegui. Ahora, usted está en Al Arabi y Julen es el seleccionador de Qatar. ¿Cómo lo ve en perspectiva? ¿Han tenido oportunidad de hablarlo desde que están aquí? R. Hemos quedado alguna que otra vez a tomar un café y charlar. Al final, esto no es muy grande y tienes la facilidad de reunirte y hablar con mucha gente. Con Lopetegui, no sólo coincidimos en las inferiores de la Selección, sino también en los Wolves. Tengo muchas experiencias con él y su cuerpo técnico. P. Se va a celebrar durante las próximas semanas el Mundial Sub17 en Qatar por segundo año consecutivo. Vuelve España… y hay materia prima para seguir nutriendo a la Absoluta. ¿Somos el mejor país formador del mundo? R. No sé si somos el mejor… pero está claro que uno de los tres mejores seguro. Estamos haciendo las cosas muy bien desde hace muchísimo tiempo. Con una filosofía muy definida. Tenemos una materia prima increíble. La labor no es sólo a nivel nacional, creo que también viene desde los equipos. Se está trabajando muy bien a nivel formativo para poder crear y desarrollar este tipo de chicos que vienen con la calidad innata… pero también hay que pulirla. P. Qatar es un país donde todo está bastante a mano. Sois 18 españoles en la Liga. ¿Hacen vida fuera del campo? R. Alguna vez nos vemos. Hay muchísima gente aquí y, si no has coincidido en un sitio, lo haces en otro. La gran virtud de vivir en Qatar es que todo se desarrolla en Doha y todos los equipos son de aquí. P. ¿Con quién tiene más relación? R. Con Luis Alberto y David García, sobre todo. Nos solemos reunir con las familias también. P. Volviendo a esa etapa en el Real Madrid, usted debutó con Mourinho. 15 años después, está de vuelta en el Bernabéu. ¿Cómo lo recuerda? Imagino que era difícil abrirse hueco en ese equipo… R. Yo a Mourinho le estaré eternamente agradecido. Él fue el responsable de que pudiese vivir uno de los días más felices de mi vida: debutar en el Bernabéu y en Champions. Con esa edad, fue increíble. Todo lo que significó para mi familia. Ver esa cara de felicidad que tenían cuando acabó el partido fue increíble. Ahora ha vuelto y yo creo que es diferente, otra etapa y otro tipo de jugadores. Ojalá haga un buen trabajo porque creo que este Madrid también se lo merece y lo necesita. P. Por aquel entonces, también compartía vestuario con Carvajal en el Castilla. Se llegó a especular con su posible llegada a Qatar. ¿Llegaron a hablar de ello? R. Tenía diferentes opciones. Todos sabemos la trayectoria de Carvajal. Equipos no le han faltado, obviamente. Al final, por algunas circunstancias, ha decidido jugar en el Getafe. Pero considero que en Qatar estarían encantados de recibir a un jugador de esa magnitud. P. Finalmente, decidió firmar por el Getafe. Usted comenzó a dar sus primeros pasos como profesional en el Coliseum. ¿Qué importancia le da a ese primer paso en su carrera? R. Fue un paso muy importante porque yo venía de jugar en 2ªB con el Real Madrid. El Getafe fue quien me dio la oportunidad de subir a Primera y estoy muy agradecido por ello. Al principio, es verdad que me costó. El ritmo era totalmente diferente. Pero, poco a poco, fui creciendo, madurando y cogiendo esa experiencia necesaria para jugar en primera. Crecí mucho durante esas cinco años. P. Posteriormente, fue al Sevilla y acabó explotando. ¿Fueron los mejores años de su trayectoria? R. Posiblemente, sí. Creo que mi período más importante fue en Getafe. Sobre todo, los dos últimos años. Mentalmente, hice un trabajo por el que, a día de hoy, estoy aquí. No fue fácil la adaptación a Primera. Ese es el punto de inflexión en mi carrera. Pero, a nivel vistoso, de disfrute y de dar un paso más, considero que esos tres años en Sevilla fueron los más felices. P. Le valió para firmar por el PSG. No muchos jugadores puede presumir de haber compartido vestuario con Messi y Cristiano. ¿Con qué se queda de cada uno? R. Cristiano es un auténtico líder. Carácter, ambición… Todos nos tendríamos que fijar en él. No sólo en el fútbol, también en cualquier ámbito de la vida. Cada uno en su trabajo tiene que intentar ser mejor cada día y ponerse metas. Cristiano quiere más cada día y ha presionado sus límites. De Messi, al final todos vemos la calidad y su manera de ver el fútbol. Su mente es diferente. Lo ve todo mucho más rápido y toma decisiones que no están al alcance de otro ser humano. P. ¿Son cercanos en el día a día? R. Sí, yo he tenido mucha suerte con ambos. Me han tratado de lujo cuando he compartido vestuario con ellos. Hemos charlado de muchísimas cosas y, al final, me han hecho sentir uno más. Siendo lo que son, esa parte humana es importantísima. P. Estuvo presente en la final contra el Bayern en 2020. ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre aquel PSG y el que viene de ser bicampeón de Europa? R. El factor ‘equipo’ hace mucho. No teníamos malos jugadores, ni mucho menos. Estábamos plagados de estrellas. Pero, hoy en día, necesitas crear un equipo por encima de las individualidades. Este PSG lo ha conseguido a la perfección con Luis Enrique. Él se considera un entrenador de equipo y le da igual lo que digan. Tiene su propia idea y la prima por encima de todo. Esa ha sido la clave. Obviamente, tienen mucha calidad. Pero el sentimiento de equipo marca la diferencia. Da igual quién seas. P. Luis Enrique le llevó a la Eurocopa y al Mundial. ¿Qué le hace diferente? R. Tiene una riqueza táctica muy buena. Sabe jugar con diferentes sistemas, leer todos los partidos que hay dentro de un mismo encuentro… y toma decisiones en función de ello. Eso enriquece el sentimiento de equipo. Le da igual quién seas. Si te sacrificas por el grupo, lo vas a tener todo. Si cree que vas por libre, no vas a tener nada. Son dos grandes virtudes. Sin entrar a valorar el nivel humano. Personalmente, tengo una gran relación con él. Pero eso es a nivel personal. P. La primera vez que pisa Qatar sale en la prórroga del Mundial 2022 contra Marruecos en octavos. Está a punto de ganar el partido… y luego falla el primer penalti. ¿Le sigue dando vueltas? R. Personalmente, me siento muy orgulloso de haber estado en un Mundial y haber podido representar a España. Lo que sucedió contra Marruecos son circunstancias del fútbol. A veces, te da… y otras te castiga. En ese momento, va al palo y no entra. En los penaltis no me arrepiento de nada. Siempre digo que falla quien lo tira. Yo asumí esa responsabilidad y lo volvería a hacer. No me arrepiento de nada. P. Su último partido con España fue contra Colombia en marzo de 2024. La última derrota de la Selección hasta la de Inglaterra. ¿Se imaginaba todo lo que vendría después con la Eurocopa, Mundial…? R. España está haciendo un gran trabajo. Las semillas ya estaban creadas desde hace tiempo para un estilo de juego muy definido. Está creciendo muchísimo la Selección. Estoy totalmente feliz de todos y cada uno de ellos. Tengo relación con algunos. Ojalá sigan jugando mucho tiempo y nos sigan dando alegrías. P. Todavía tiene 34 años. No sé cómo de lejos ve la retirada, pero… ¿su intención es colgar las botas en Qatar? R. Me gusta disfrutar del día a día. Disfrutar del fútbol, que es lo que más feliz me hace. A partir de ahí, ya veremos cómo vamos avanzando y dónde acabamos. Pero la verdad es que estoy muy feliz en Qatar. Estoy disfrutando y mi familia también. Creo que hay posibilidad de estar aquí un poco más de tiempo.

articles.title: Ecuadorian footballer gets eight-year ban for throwing rock at referee
articles.summary: Jhon Perlaza threw a stone that struck an assistant referee, who later required surgery, during a third-tier match.
articles.body:
Football authorities in Ecuador have handed an eight-year ban to player Jhon Perlaza after ⁠he threw a stone that struck an assistant referee during a third-tier match last month.

“The assistant referee suffered serious injuries that required surgery and a 60-day recovery period,” ‌Ecuador’s football ‌federation (FEF) said in a statement announcing the sanction on Wednesday.

The incident occurred ⁠during the 96th minute of the match between Perlaza’s side Club Ciudad de Yantzaza and Club Rio Aguarico ⁠FC on October 17. The match was abandoned after assistant referee Lenin Giovanni Ojeda Nunez was struck.

“The disciplinary committee found the player responsible for physical aggression against a match official and suspended him for eight years from all football-related activity, until October 19, 2034.

“In addition, the FEF will ask FIFA to extend this ⁠sanction worldwide.”

The FEF added that Yantzaza would ⁠have to pay a fine of $2,000 as well as a further $4,369.73 to cover the assistant referee’s medical expenses.

In a statement released on October ⁠20, Yantzaza apologised to the refereeing team and fans for the incident.

“As an institution, ⁠we categorically reject all acts of ⁠aggression, whether verbal or physical, both inside and outside sporting venues. We firmly believe that football should be a space of respect, coexistence, and ‌fair play,” they said.

“Once the person responsible for this regrettable incident was identified, the institution made the decision ‌to ‌remove him immediately, and he is therefore no longer part of our club.”

articles.title: BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026: Cast your vote
articles.summary: Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal are shortlisted for the BBC's Men's Footballer of the Year award.
articles.body:
Voting is now open for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year.

Fans from the UK can vote from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal.

The vote closes on Friday, 27 November at 09:00 GMT.

The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December.

Alex Kay-Jelski, Director of BBC Sport, said: "From the drama and excitement of the men's World Cup to the moments that have captivated fans across the domestic and international game, 2026 has given us so much to celebrate.

"Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game.

"It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner."

The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game.

The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales).

Bellingham made history this summer as he became the first Englishman to score as many as seven goals at a major tournament.

In a superb World Cup for the midfielder, he memorably netted twice in back-to-back games to help the Three Lions beat Mexico and Norway.

That meant he joined exalted company as the first player to score two or more goals in successive World Cup knockout games since Diego Maradona in 1986, and the second youngest in history behind Pele in 1958.

Bellingham also became the youngest European player to make an appearance at four different major tournaments, and also reached the milestone of 50 caps at a younger age than any other England men's player.

The goals continued to flow for Real Madrid, too, with Bellingham notching his 50th for the club to move above the legendary Zinedine Zidane in the Los Blancos' all-time scoring charts.

In a stunning year of goalscoring, Kane become the first Englishman for 25 years (and only fifth in history) to win the Ballon d'Or - awarded to the world's best footballer.

His tally of 73 goals in 65 matches for club and country during a stellar 2025-26 season has only been surpassed in one of Europe's top five leagues by Lionel Messi's 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12.

Kane scored 61 of those goals in just 51 appearances for Bayern Munich as he helped the Bavarians to a league and cup double. His total was 19 more than any other player in Europe's top five divisions.

Already England's record goalscorer, he surpassed Peter Shilton's mark of 125 appearances to become the most-capped Englishman in history.

Six goals at this summer's World Cup also helped him overtake Gary Lineker as the Three Lions' record scorer at the tournament, while he joined David Beckham as the only Englishmen to score in three separate World Cups.

Mbappe came out on top of an enthralling tussle with Lionel Messi at the 2026 World Cup to become the leading goalscorer in the tournament's history.

The France forward, who is still only 27, took his tally to 22 from just three World Cups to finish one ahead of the great Argentine.

Mbappe's 10 goals from eight games this summer meant he won his second World Cup Golden Boot - a feat no player has managed before.

It also made him the first man to reach double figures at a World Cup since Gerd Muller in 1970, with only Just Fontaine (13) and Sandor Kocsis (11) having scored more goals in a single tournament.

Other achievements in a standout year included him finishing runner-up in the Ballon d'Or awards and overtaking Olivier Giroud as France's all-time leading goalscorer.

He scored 25 times to retain his title as La Liga's top scorer during a 2025-26 campaign in which he netted 42 goals in all competitions for Real Madrid.

Midfield maestro Rodri earned yet another accolade in his incredible career when he was awarded the Golden Ball trophy for the World Cup's best player.

By captaining Spain to glory in the US, Rodri became only the fourth male player to win the World Cup, European Championship, Champions League and Ballon d'Or - following in the footsteps of legendary Germans Gerd Muller and Franz Beckenbauer and France's Zinedine Zidane.

His achievements were made all the more special given doubts remained over whether he would recapture his best form after a long recovery from a serious knee injury in 2024.

Then Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola predicted he would return to his best at the World Cup and he was right. Rodri completed 756 passes there - the most in the tournament since records began in 1966.

His final season at Manchester City before departing for Barcelona ended in familiar fashion with a domestic cup double taking his trophy haul with the club to 14.

Lamine Yamal continues to rewrite the record books with his astonishing exploits for club and country.

Just days after his 19th birthday, the Spaniard became the youngest footballer to have played in - and won - both a World Cup and a European Championship. The only players younger than him to play in a World Cup final are Brazil's Pele in 1958 and Giuseppe Bergomi for Italy in 1982.

For the second year running, his performances led to a podium place at the Ballon d'Or and at the same award ceremony he became the first footballer in history to win the Young Talent of the Year three years in succession.

At club level, he was named La Liga's Best Player courtesy of a starring role in Barcelona's title success. The teenager ended the season with an impressive 24 goals and 18 assists across all competitions.

He recently broke Kylian Mbappe's record for the most goals by a teenager in Champions League history.

articles.body:
Are Man City in crisis heading into Saturday lunchtime's clash against Fulham, with Enzo Maresca's side having lost their previous three Premier League contests to lose top spot to Arsenal?

Those trio of reverses against Aston Villa, Brighton and, just prior to the international break, Nottingham Forest, mean City have now lost as many times as in their previous 36 league outings.

Since the start of 2007-08, though, City have only been beaten in four successive top-flight games on two occasions, in August 2008 and December 2024, and it would take a massive leap of faith to suggest Fulham are the team to inflict such ignominy on them this weekend.

In fact, if Maresca could pick one side to face to get back to winning ways, it would be Fulham, who City have got the better of in each of their last 17 Premier League encounters, scoring at least twice each time. Rich Morgan

Aston Villa left for the international break on a sour note after squandering a two-goal lead on two occasions at Old Trafford for their dramatic 4-4 draw against Manchester United.

Sunderland, meanwhile, secured a much-needed 1-0 win against Chelsea to relieve the pressure on Regis Le Bris.

His side remain in the bottom three because of their poor start to the season and a win at Villa Park is a big ask, especially given injuries to Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey, but it will be needed if talks of his departure are going to fizzle out.

The Black Cats have not travelled well this term with just one win on the road, which came in their narrow escape at Portuguese second-tier side Torreense, but Villa Park's crackling atmosphere has been dampened by the closure of the North Stand this season.

Injuries, storylines and ramifications. Plus, if it is anything like their last meeting at Villa Park, a dramatic 4-3 win for Villa courtesy of Tammy Abraham's injury-time winner, then this is one you will be wanting to follow along in the Sky Sports live blog. Pat Rowe

The managerial merry-go-round is spinning again. Crystal Palace have jumped aboard, handing Thomas Frank the keys to Selhurst Park. New hope. But a new manager doesn't necessarily mean new results.

In fact, recent evidence suggests quite the opposite for teams in trouble.

The famous 'new manager bounce' is one of football's most romanticised theories. A fresh face walks through the door, standards supposedly rise overnight and points start rolling in.

Of the last six Premier League teams sitting in the bottom eight to change manager between November and March, five actually saw their points-per-game average drop across the following five matches.

Vitor Pereira at Nottingham Forest. Igor Tudor at Tottenham. Rob Edwards at Wolves. Graham Potter at West Ham. Ivan Juric at Southampton.

It's a fascinating trend that should serve as a warning to Palace supporters expecting Frank to arrive waving a magic wand.

The reality is that struggling teams usually have deep-rooted problems that can't be solved by a few tactical tweaks and an inspirational team talk. Confidence, structure and, ultimately, quality of players tend to outweigh a difference voice in the dugout.

Coventry are next up for Palace and Frank will be desperate to buck the trend.

But history suggests the bounce might be more of a bump. Lewis Jones

Bournemouth couldn't buy a Premier League victory in the opening six weeks or so of the season, but over the last month they have looked like an unstoppable force. Now they can't stop winning.

Since a 3-0 win over Sturm Graz in the Europa League on October 15, the Cherries have won four in a row in the Premier League, three in a row in Europe and once in the Carabao Cup, booking a spot in the quarter-finals.

Eight wins in succession in all competitions; a club record equalled.

It's made even more astonishing when you realise Marco Rose has only been in charge for 16 games. And that it's the club's first ever season in Europe. And that those eight wins came within a period of just 25 days.

With the schedule that lies ahead, the run will naturally come under threat sooner rather than later, but where's the harm in trying to squeeze out one more win to make history? Dan Long

Ipswich have a Julio Enciso problem. Not because the Paraguayan isn't delivering the goods. Quite the opposite. He's become so influential to their attacking output that stopping him is the key to stopping Ipswich.

Bournemouth certainly cracked it before the international break.

Their 2-1 victory over Ipswich was a tactical lesson in how to suffocate a team reliant on one creative spark. Cut off the supply lines into Enciso, deny him the space to weave his magic and ask the rest of the Ipswich attack to come up with the answers.

The numbers were quite staggering. Despite trailing for almost the entire game, Ipswich created just 0.30 worth of expected goals. Even more damning was their inability to register a single touch inside the Bournemouth penalty area in the second half until the 73rd minute, when Jack Clarke scored from the penalty spot.

And that should concern O'Neil, who has seen his team win just one of their last five games in the Premier League.

Ipswich's solid start to the season has been built on some encouraging foundations, but the Premier League is a ruthless environment for teams that become predictable. Opposition analysts will have watched that Bournemouth performance with great interest.

Tottenham are next up and the blueprint is there for them to follow.

O'Neil needs other avenues of attack. Otherwise that promising start could unravel rather quickly. Lewis Jones

Chelsea and Leeds will reignite their six-decade-long rivalry on Saturday with both sides at a crossroads in their seasons.

Inconsistency has dogged each in their pursuit of better things in the opening 10 games of the campaign, but Chelsea's looks particularly apparent after their 1-0 defeat at then-bottom club Sunderland before the international break.

That result should have been as much a surprise for failing to score against their previously porous hosts as it was returning empty-handed, given their own free-scoring start to the campaign.

But not only have they managed to back up one win with another just twice in the league since Xabi Alonso's arrival, they have now failed to score in half of their last six games.

Even with the loss of the influential Joao Pedro from their patented 'JP Morgan' front three, that inconsistency is something Alonso must address quickly.

The decision to start Pedro Neto as a False 9 against Sunderland's low block was an odd one, and played out as such with the Portugal forward failing to register a single touch in the Black Cats box before he was hooked for Danny Welbeck shortly after the hour mark.

The Blues could have been three points off second had they won that game and may still be able to end the weekend in the top four should they do so against Leeds. But Alonso must find that sweet spot quickly before the table turns less forgiving. Ron Walker

Premier League titles are not won in November but Arsenal face Newcastle, live on Sky Sports on Saturday, knowing they could join a handful of sides in the history of the competition to hit the 30-point mark after only 11 games of a campaign.

The only sides to have achieved the feat up until now are Manchester City in 2017/18 and 2011/12, Liverpool in 2019/20 and Chelsea 2005/06. It should be noted that each of them went on to win the title, finishing an average of 11 points clear at the top.

Arsenal, who have won every game this season bar their 3-0 reverse at Brighton in September, have not found it easy at St James' Park in recent years. They needed two late goals to win there last term and lost three straight games there before that.

But the Magpies are at a low ebb as Matthias Jaissle struggles to get his ideas across, with only one win in five Premier League home games this term and seemingly vulnerable. Arsenal, five points clear already, will aim to take advantage and continue their charge. Nick Wright

Are Brighton the only team capable of stopping Arsenal from running away with the Premier League title? It's a question that would have sounded rather bonkers a few months ago. Not anymore.

A return of 22 points from their opening 10 games, backed up by excellent underlying numbers. Arsenal have already been beaten. This is a team playing with the swagger, confidence and control of genuine title contenders. This is no ordinary start from Fabian Hurzeler's side.

And at the heart of it all is Pascal Gross. The man has a football brain that operates on an entirely different frequency to most mere mortals.

Only Erling Haaland and Evanilson have registered more Premier League goal involvements than Gross, who has eight to his name, including four assists. But even those numbers don't do justice to his influence.

Nobody in the Premier League has created more chances (29) or big chances (8).

He sees passes before defenders have even realised there's danger. There are quicker players. More explosive players. But very few who think the game quite like Gross.

And Brighton are reaping the rewards. Lewis Jones

What is one sure-fire way to win over Manchester United fans as a new head coach? Beat Liverpool at Anfield.

That is, of course, easier said than done. But what a statement it would be for Mauricio Pochettino if he could pull it off.

The Argentine's appointment feels like it's been years in the making, yet has also come at a time when his stock is lower than it was when he was previously linked with the Old Trafford hot seat. Had United appointed any other manager of the USMNT, they may have been ridiculed.

However, Pochettino comes with undeniable Premier League pedigree. He just needs to show that he still has that magic touch. His players are expected to be put through their paces with his fitness-first approach. Even for a team with some of the worst running stats in the division, putting a shift in on Merseyside should not be an issue. On the contrary, it's a prerequisite. If they don't, then it's a major mark against Pochettino in just his first few days at the helm.

Perhaps his task shouldn't be to try and win the game. He will probably be forgiven for not. But his team have to put in a performance that epitomises what the Pochettino era is supposed to look like. If he needs an example, look no further than January at Michael Carrick's first two games in charge. Arguably his two best.

If there is a level of work ethic on and off the ball that mirror those games against Manchester City and Arsenal, the new regime will earn supporters among the doubters. Add a win to the equation, and the Stretford End may well be signing 'Poch is at the wheel' come the time to face Brentford six days later. Callum Bishop

Anyone who attended a game at Griffin Park any time before about 2018 and has had their head buried firmly in the sand since may be surprised to hear this, but…

There is a feeling that Brentford Football Club, sat eighth in the Premier League, might just be underperforming in the early part of this season.

The Bees have just three wins all season, all at home, with too many draws on the road halting their progress under Keith Andrews.

It may be in part due to Igor Thiago. His 22 goals last season so often proved the difference in tight games for Brentford. But he doesn't look the same confident striker he was last season in front of goal, with just two in 10 so far - and neither being decisive in terms of the result.

They will be without him for the clash with Everton after his red card against Brighton before the international break.

He had previously started 47 of Keith Andrews' 48 games in charge of the club, and now he will have the chance to experiment with some different options in attack.

Callum Wilson, who has scored three times in the Carabao Cup so far this season, could be handed a first Premier League start after seven substitute appearances totalling just 56 minutes of action. Simeon Gholam

articles.title: Ronaldo, Henry, Kane, Haaland: The best European strikers this century - voted by you
articles.summary: BBC Sport reveals the top 10 European strikers this century, as voted for by you.
articles.body:
Classic number nines, penalty-box poachers, troublesome targetmen and tireless all-rounders.

There is no one-size fits all when it comes to determining great strikers, but they do all share a common trait - a ruthlessness in front of goal.

This week, however, we put the power in your hands to decide the best European frontmen of the 21st century.

Tens of thousands of you voted on the 20-man shortlist drawn up by our panel.

We then asked European football experts Guillem Balague, Julien Laurens and Raphael Honigstein to discuss your choices on the Euro Leagues podcast.

So from 10-1, here are the best European strikers this century - as voted for by you.

Top 10 European Strikers of the Century - Part One

Karim Benzema comes in at number 10, the former Lyon and Real Madrid frontman's closest challengers coming from across the continent in the shape of Raul, Robin van Persie, Michael Owen and Miroslav Klose.

Laurens: "From a young age you could see he was something special. I know it was difficult at the beginning at Real Madrid, but in the post-Cristiano era he carried that team, wore the armband and won big titles and trophies by being decisive in big moments. Like I used to say 'Karim the dream'."

Honigstein: "The selflessness, the ability to work for the team. A sense of elegance and humility on the pitch, which is unusual in a goalscorer. I think he is unusual in that list. I think not many will define themselves through their teamwork and assists as much as their goals, but he was that player."

Ruud van Nistelrooy edges Benzema, with whom he briefly overlapped at Real Madrid - the Dutchman teed up the Frenchman and scored himself in their only La Liga appearance together, before he left for Hamburg in January 2010 following injury problems.

The former PSV striker's most consistent spell, of course, came at Manchester United, where he scored 150 goals.

Honigstein: "He is the nicest guy but he never came across that way on the pitch. Typical trait of a striker, he would kill to score the goal. I think anyone who has grown up with him scoring goals, for United especially, must have a soft spot for him because he was a phenomenal poacher."

Laurens: "He was a strong player physically, and despite the lack of pace the awareness in the box was just very special even with all the injuries."

Zlatan Ibrahimovic slots in at eight, comfortably clear of Van Nistelrooy and Benzema. The Swede netted more than 500 times in a career that spanned Malmo, Ajax, Juventus, both Milans, Barcelona, Paris St-Germain, Manchester United and LA Galaxy.

Balague: "He was a big-game player and that explains the league titles with PSG. Scoring four goals against England, the overhead kick. The personality thing has put him one or two places in this list, saying 'I am great, I am the best'. If you keep saying you're great it makes people stop and think."

Laurens: "The mentality of really believing he was the best and nobody was better than him, apart from maybe Brazilian Ronaldo, who was his idol growing up, and he would watch videos of him and try to replicate in his council estate. If you watch a highlight reel of his best goals he was incredible."

Honigstein: "What makes him unique among the strikers is his technique, You could see elements of martial arts in his goals. No-one scores goals like that."

The first Englishman on the list, although the third to have represented Manchester United - it's the Old Trafford outfit's record goalscorer, Wayne Rooney.

Honigstein: "I don't think there is anyone who would've watched English football at that time [early in his career] and not been enthralled by his game. The only downside is the combination of injuries and not the most professional lifestyle meant he did not fulfil his potential. He could've been Messi."

Balague: "What could have been, yes. He was the national team's record scorer too before Harry Kane took it. I find him to deserve this place as he had to adapt to a lot of strikers and he did it well. He had the ability to link up and score. He was very intelligent."

Laurens: "He is the most street footballer England has ever seen. There's no rules, that kind of anger you saw on the pitch. I don't think people in England realise how good he was."

What does becoming the all-time World Cup top goalscorer get you? Sixth place on the best European strikers this century list. The Real Madrid forward, 27, just misses out on the top five.

Laurens: "Maybe if we do this ranking again in a few years he will be higher. I would have had him top five, for sure. He has scored more than 400 goals. I don't think Messi and Ronaldo had scored that many at that age, so he's ahead. I don't know if he will play for as long as them but he hasn't done much wrong in his career."

Balague: "This list has to do what you feel about the player, not science - 22 goals in 22 appearances in World Cups and [Euro] Championships. He should be at least top three because of that. Great stats, but we're not in love with him."

Honigstein: " I don't think there is a forward that is as good as footballer as him in 2026. On that basis alone he should be higher, but people when they vote have other things in their head. The only way to win everyone over is to score more goals and win more World Cups for France, which I think is possible."

There was little between Mbappe and Erling Haaland, but it is Manchester City's prolific Norwegian who slips in at fifth. The 26-year-old has already scored more than 300 club goals and has a staggering 68 in 61 games for his country.

Balague: "Mbappe should be higher than him. Haaland scored 52 goals in 53 games [in 2022-23], that is astonishing, but he's gone 11 finals without scoring. We're talking about the best. We're talking about what we see at the moment and what we see is someone who is calculated but in a more charming way. An ability to score we haven't seen in a while; power, ability to finish. He is not world class to the level of others."

Honigstein: "I don't think it's fair to judge him on just that. They [Manchester City] won the Champions League when he was there. When Haaland arrived with Pep Guardiola, they found a way to do it. What makes him unique is the physical attributes and the pace. To have both is unique. He can sprint like a 100m sprinter. Is he the fifth best striker of the 21st Century? I don't think he's that far behind."

Interesting, this, because Robert Lewandowski is well clear of Haaland in fourth, but the leap from the Polish forward to the top three is massive - more than 10,000 votes.

The 38-year-old is still chipping away for Chicago Fire in Major League Soccer, having been a reliably ruthless assassin for Barcelona, Bayern and Dortmund.

Honigstein: "He used to play basketball, judo, handball - his father wanted him to have a wholesome education. You could see his completeness that he had as a centre-forward. Nothing in his game was extraordinary but in terms of ticking all the boxes, none come close to him."

Balague: "He said he learned to be an elite striker when he forgot what he had just done, like a fish. Mistakes he had in his head affected his performance. One day he just continued like it didn't matter."

Laurens: "He won the Ballon d'Or in Covid, it won't be on his mantlepiece but we all know it was his."

Fresh from his Ballon d'Or triumph, England's record goalscorer and appearance maker rides into the top three on the back of 61 goals in 51 outings for Bayern Munich last season.

Kane left the Premier League three years ago with the second-most goals ever in the competition, and is also Tottenham's all-time record scorer.

Honigstein: "Third place, at least. He is doing incredible things. At 33, still not quite at his peak. I don't think he relies on his pace, physicality, it's all about intelligence, technique. I don't think there's anyone in the game that strikes a ball as well as him right now. I don't think any player comes close that we've talked about so far in overall work-rate, defending, helping the team, making tackles in your box in the 90th minute when you're 3-0 up because he's that kind of guy. He is humble and a superb human being."

Laurens: "What I love about Kane, from a young age, a lot of this list you just knew the trajectory would be all the way to the top. Kane was not like that. It could have been very different for him. Nobody at 17 would've said he was going to win the Ballon d'Or. Nobody believed in him like the others. Kane had a very different journey."

Runner-up Thierry Henry is the only striker in the top six who is retired. A World Cup and Euros winner with France, Henry won titles with Arsenal - where he scored 228 goals - and a Champions League with Barcelona.

Honigstein: "During his time, I don't think there was a player like him in the Premier League. The way he played football was stylish, elegant, but there was almost a kind of a romantic connection between him and the ball. I don't think there was anyone near that kind of level of technique and, for want of a better word, va-va-voom he exuded. That just made for amazing viewing."

Laurens: "For me as a fellow Parisien, he's a very special player, a very special man. A career that has been incredible from a young age. It's that season in the Premier League - 24 goals, 20 assists in 38 games - not even Kane or Benzema or Cristiano, OK, Messi is different, but they haven't done that and yet he did it.

"There are still some people who undervalue him and underappreciate him and the monster that he was on the football pitch. He had it all. The pace, the style, the elegance, the technique, the mentality, the goals, the aura, the charisma. Just everything you wanted if you were to build a striker. One of the greatest football brains ever."

Of course, at number one, it's the man chasing the 1,000-goal dream. Cristiano Ronaldo may have retired from Portugal duty with 146 notches on his strike chart but the quest goes on at Al-Nassr.

The 41-year-old's evolution from tricky winger to prolific frontman has taken him from Sporting to Manchester United, twice, Real Madrid, Juventus and now Saudi Arabia.

Balague: "He's the best striker in history. His numbers are incredible. He won't stop until he gets to 1,000. He is somebody who is special. We know his background, how he wanted to be Ballon d'Or winner at 12 and didn't stop until he got there. He ran up the mountains of Funchal with weights in his ankles and snuck into the gym when it was closed to get the physique he wanted."

Laurens: "Always in the right place at the right time. The instinct. He was born with a gift, like all in this list. But you still have to work hard. Nobody will ever reach those levels again. 1,000 goals for club and country will never be done again, I think."

Honigstein: "Peak Ronaldo for me was Gareth Bale scoring and him looking very unhappy. I don't think there will be any dispute about him being the greatest. Somebody who has done it all, won it all, and he's still going for the love of it."

articles.title: Man City vs Fulham: Has Enzo Fernandez given Enzo Maresca a problem in midfield? And how does he fix the imbalance?
articles.summary: Man City have lost their last three Premier League games on the bounce; Enzo Maresca's most used midfield pairing are yet to gel and signs are that their profiles are incompatible; should Enzo Fernandez be dropped altogether or would a higher role suit him and Maresca's system better?
articles.body:
Maresca began with seven straight wins in all competitions. He has since suffered a hat-trick of Premier League defeats. Concerns over performance levels in certain phases existed from the start but have come into sharper focus as results have nosedived.

Stylistically, City are far too open; just as easy to play through as play over. Only Newcastle (20) have faced more shots from fast breaks since the start of term than City's 17, conceding two goals from such situations in defeat to Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Transition moments have been City's kryptonite long before the Maresca era. However their current setup leaves them vulnerable to the problem persisting - or worsening. The make-up of Elliot Anderson in a double pivot with Enzo Fernandez is a poor stylistic fit if Rayan Cherki is selected as the other central player. It's too easy to overrun.

Cherki offers virtually nothing out of possession, which is ok if the two deeper lying midfielders work against the ball in tandem. At City this is not the case. Fernandez's positioning and ineffectiveness in duels leaves Anderson far too isolated and even he - one of the team's most reliable performers - got caught at Forest, at fault for Liam Delap's first goal.

City conceded eight fast breaks in total; no team has conceded more in a game this season.

Positionally, Anderson and Fernandez have a tendency to drift into similar areas, both active on the right side of City's midfield. Per 90, the Argentine is tackling less and winning possession less frequently than he did at Chelsea, over-exposing the central third. His offensive numbers do little to make up for the deficit.

At the City Ground, Xaver Schlager and Ryan Yates lapped up the imbalance. Schlager registered a game-high 14 defensive contributions (measured as clearances, blocks, interceptions, and tackles), while Yates racked up 11. Fernandez's tally was four, less than Cherki's five from the bench.

Maresca is taking a big risk playing both. The difficulty is of course also exacerbated by the fact City spent over £320m rebuilding their midfield unit this summer and, so far, the profile of their two hero £100m-plus signings have proved incompatible. That headache is Maresca's to solve.

The Italian is not in the business of copying the model his Spanish predecessor made so successful in his 10 years at City but in this instance it might be worth asking: What would Pep Guardiola do?

Pep teams always created numerical and positional overloads in midfield. Bernardo Silva was the master of such an art and in that sense, has arguably been a greater loss to the City dynamic than Rodri has. Theoretically, pairing Bernardo with Anderson would alleviate many of the out-of-possession mistakes the team are currently making. The issue is a macro one.

And so if City are craving another ball-winner to build greater stability from the base of midfield, one who can also play under pressure, Ayyoub Bouaddi is the obvious choice. The teenager has been under utilised in the league, only managing 177 minutes, and has now had time to settle into his new surroundings.

Bouaddi is a physical presence with great athleticism and would reduce the defensive emphasis on Anderson. He would also have a greater level of positional discipline than Fernandez and therefore adds another layer of resistance against the ball.

For a side who have lacked control and been exposed via structural gaps by the likes of Sunderland, Ipswich and most recently Forest, extra cover is an easy tweak for a quick win. Bouaddi is a readymade screening No 6.

But packing the midfield does not necessarily mean dropping the player Maresca pushed so hard to sign just two-and-a-half months ago. If this is an exercise in balance, Fernandez at the tip of a midfield triangle could work as an alternative to Cherki - depending on the game plan. This is still a team that thrives in possession and can score from almost anywhere.

Fernandez holds up the ball well, draws fouls, crashes the box with decent timing and can create as well as he can finish. He's yet to score from open play for City but can offer plenty in a free role with adequate cover in behind. Of course the creative merits of Cherki in that function deserve consideration too - but Maresca surely needs to prioritise solidity through his spine given the predicament.

City play Fulham this weekend, having won their last 17 games against them, scoring at least twice each time. This time last year Pep's City shipped four goals at Craven Cottage and yet still ended on the winning side of a 5-4 thriller. Maresca cannot afford to take that gamble.

He must find a way to better protect the backline in transition moments. Or City risk this brand of chaos over control taking permanent hold of a season that already has its fair share of intractable problems.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino at Man Utd: Seven years on from the sack at Spurs what sort of coach is he now? We will soon find out
articles.summary: Seven years on from being sacked by Tottenham Hotspur, Mauricio Pochettino is back in the Premier League with Manchester United with an impressive reputation but a point to prove. Adam Bate asks whether he can roll back the years and deliver at Old Trafford...
articles.body:
In his five full seasons in charge, Spurs were in the Premier League's top five each time - a run that has never been bettered in their history. He took the club above Arsenal for the first time in a generation and into a Champions League final for the first time ever.

Silverware was missing, much to the amusement of his critics, but the charges against Manchester City serve as a reminder that he was playing with the deck stacked against him. He overachieved and it is his thrilling football that endures in the memory.

The arc of history has bent towards his intense style of play.

He is an obvious upgrade for Manchester United, a club that lurched from one error to the next but somehow appointed only one manager with Premier League experience in over a decade - and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's brief time at Cardiff hardly merited the job.

And yet, Pochettino, for all his undoubted charm - something that has helped to earn him so many vocal admirers in the media - still comes with a question mark. There is a point to prove here because that time at Tottenham ended exactly seven years ago.

Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal have since been characterised as yesterday's men even upon their arrival, the former somewhat incongruously so now given that he is currently being deployed back on the bench at a little known outfit called Real Madrid.

But Mourinho came to United two years on from a Premier League title. For Van Gaal it would be his final club job. And yet, even he was fresh from a rather better World Cup and had taken Bayern Munich to a Champions League final four years prior not seven.

Pochettino has hardly been thumb twiddling in that time. There was a title win with Paris Saint-Germain, albeit at the second attempt. Some talk up his work with the United States. Others see particular parallels in how he navigated a tricky situation at Chelsea.

That chaos could prepare him well for his new assignment.

There is an argument that rather than his football ideas being compromised by these various challenges, he is a more rounded coach as a result. Player power will hardly be new to a man who had to field a front line of Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Neymar.

Try getting those three to press the opposition.

Nevertheless, it is his accomplishments in constructing that Tottenham team that give the greatest cause for excitement. Can he build a side like that again? Does he even want to given that the Pochettino stamp has been less evident in his subsequent work?

In those first six seasons as a Premier League manager, Pochettino's teams never ranked lower than third for PPDA, the recognised metric for pressing. His Tottenham were pressing monsters, just as Espanyol and Southampton had been before that.

In his final four full seasons at Spurs, his sides never ranked lower than third for distance covered either. But his Chelsea team ranked among the bottom three on the same metric. It is indicative of how he has had to find a different way to get results.

That will certainly be the case at United, at least initially. He inherits a group of players ill-suited to the football that made him famous. As Pochettino's predecessor put it so memorably: "If you don't run forward and you don't run back, you aren't going to win."

The good news is that his reputation should buy him some time and trust. Enough for Pochettino's ideas to emerge. He has not done two years in a club job since Spurs and is now clutching a contract that should keep him at Manchester United until the summer of 2029.

Patience will be needed. One recalls one of his final interviews with Sky Sports during that time in charge of Tottenham, when the tempo began to slow and the vibrancy of his football lost some of its lustre. Those words seem just as relevant to the United of today.

"With a team that plays in the Champions League, a team in which 90 per cent of the players play for their national sides, it is important to remember how important pre-seasons are," he told Sky Sports . "This year, we did not have the stability and we started working late."

It is worth remembering that before he built that dynamic Spurs side led by Harry Kane, he had to chip away to construct the team. In that first season, he called on Federico Fazio and Vlad Chiriches, Etienne Capoue and Paulinho, Roberto Soldado and Emmanuel Adebayor.

At United, the turnaround in personnel and fortunes will need to be even greater. It is a mammoth task but this could still be the job of his life, even if Pochettino is already a decade older than Sir Alex Ferguson was when he arrived. Maybe they are made for each other...

Club and coach are looking to roll back the years.

articles.title: Pick of the stats: Lincoln City v Wrexham
articles.summary: BBC Sport highlights some of the key stats and facts for the Championship match between Lincoln City and Wrexham.
articles.body:
Lincoln will seek to pull away from the Championship drop-zone when they welcome Wrexham on Saturday (15:00 GMT).

The Imps are five points clear of third-bottom Burnley after a run of six defeats in eight games and have taken only five points from their seven home games so far.

The Red Dragons are three points but six places ahead of their hosts after taking four points from two home games against Middlesbrough and Wolves before the break but have taken only two from their past five away games and scored just once in that run.

Having been unbeaten in eight consecutive Football League home games against Wrexham between 1989 and 2005, Lincoln have now lost each of the past three.

Wrexham have won their past six Football League games against Lincoln – only against Bradford Park Avenue (9 between 1966 and 1970) and Oxford United (7 between 1999 and 2005) have they had longer runs.

Lincoln have lost six of their past eight league games (W1 D1), including the last three in a row. They last lost four consecutively in December 2023/January 2024.

Wrexham are winless in their past five away league games (D2 L3), scoring just one goal in that run. They've lost their past two on the road, last losing three in a row in February 2024.

Lincoln have played the highest share of their passes long in the Championship this season (24.7%), while they rank bottom for possession (36.9%), passing accuracy (68.7%) and successful passes per game (193).
